note: Authored against the FIXTURE transcripts, not real speech. The owned
catalogue points at a test stream with no audio, so the pipeline ran a
fixture transcriber and these questions were written by reading its
output.
What this set can and cannot measure:
MEANINGFUL — refusal accuracy. An out-of-scope question is out of scope
whatever the corpus, so the refuse/answer decision is genuinely under
test.
MEANINGFUL — citation timestamp accuracy. The expected timestamps are
read from the actual chunk boundaries, so this measures whether a
citation lands on the moment it claims. That is the §11.1 property the
whole layer's credibility rests on, and it is corpus-independent.
PARTIALLY MEANINGFUL — retrieval precision. Questions paraphrase rather
than quote the transcript, so retrieval must do semantic work. But the
fixture vocabulary is small and repetitive, which makes it easier than
real speech.
NOT MEANINGFUL — cross-video comparison. Every fixture transcript is
identical, so there is nothing to compare across talks. The category is
present and empty rather than filled with cases that would score well
and prove nothing.
ABSENT — non-English, per §17 decision 3 (English only).
This set becomes invalid the moment real transcripts are loaded. The
runner enforces that rather than trusting anyone to remember.
